extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers, naturalists, and scholars of natural history and ethnography
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and constructing scientific accounts of the geographical distribution of plants, animals, and human races — including classificatory principles, climatic correlations, historical/geological explanation, and the use (and limits) of linguistic and anatomical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific treatment of plant geography
rubrics_metrics.description: A scientific treatment of the subject begins when the geography of plants is intimately associated with the study of the distribution of heat over the surface of the earth, and when the arrangement of vegetable forms in natural families admits of a numerical estimate being made of the different forms which increase or decrease as we recede from the equator toward the poles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: correlate plant distributions with climate (especially heat distribution), organize plants into natural families, and quantify changes in species numbers with latitude/elevation to produce rigorous scientific analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of isothermal and isochimenal lines to explain species limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The curves of the isothermal lines, and more especially those of the isochimenal lines, correspond with the limits which are seldom passed by certain species of plants, and of animals which do not wander far from their fixed habitation either with respect to elevation or latitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: map thermal and seasonal temperature curves and compare them with species ranges — thermal geography is a principal explanatory tool for distribution limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish 'representative' vs 'identical' species in biogeographical evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Naturalists have not hitherto sufficiently distinguished between the evidence of the law, as exhibited by 'representative species' and by 'identical'. In reality, the former essentially depend on the law, the latter being an 'accident' not necessarily dependent upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting parallels between mountain and latitudinal zones, evaluate whether similarity arises from representative (closely related but distinct) species reflecting the law, or from identical species that may require independent historical/transport explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for geological history and transport mechanisms when identical species occur
rubrics_metrics.description: In several cases the presence of identical species at distant points could not be accounted for by ordinary modes of transportation now in action; one must consider means that introduced sub-Arctic (mountain) floras into regions, the vast area swept by the glacial sea, and belts of land since uplifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconstruct past geological/climatic conditions (glaciation, land bridges, uplift) and consider ancient transport processes before concluding on origins of identical disjunct populations; use geological and botanical probabilities together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate plant and animal dispersal/mobility in distribution studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants migrate in the germ; seeds are furnished with organs adapting them to be conveyed at a distance through the air; when once they have taken root they become dependent on the soil and air strata. Animals, on the contrary, can at pleasure migrate from the equator toward the poles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: in explanations, treat plants primarily as passive dispersers (seed-based) constrained by establishment conditions, and animals as active migrants — this affects interpretation of range shifts and responses to climatic gradients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate floras by coexistence and relative numerical composition rather than single-family predominance
rubrics_metrics.description: The character of the floras ... consists not so much in the relatively larger number of the species presented by one or two natural families, as in the more complicated relations of the coexistence of many families, and in the relative numerical value of their species. The predominance of certain forms is often only apparent, owing to the aspect imparted by social plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid judging regional floras solely by the most conspicuous families; quantify species numbers across families and analyze patterns of coexistence and relative abundance to assess 'luxuriance' or 'poverty' of vegetation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit geographical denominations and prefer small familial groupings in racial classification
rubrics_metrics.description: In the determination of races a preference should be given to the establishment of small families of nations. Whether we adopt Blumenbach's five races or Prichard's seven, we fail to recognize any typical sharpness of definition ... geographical denominations are very vague when used to express the points of departure of races.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify human varieties at a finer-grained (smaller family) level rather than forcing broad continental labels; be wary of using geographic names as fixed racial categories because of historical population movements and mixed ancestry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intermediate gradations, analogies, and hybrid fertility as evidence for unity of the human species
rubrics_metrics.description: More powerful reasons can be advanced in support of the theory of the unity of the human race, as, for instance, in the many intermediate gradations in the color of the skin and in the form of the skull, the analogies presented by the varieties in the species of many wild and domesticated animals, and the more correct observations collected regarding the limits of fecundity in hybrids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arguing for common descent or unity, marshal evidence of continuous morphological gradations, correspondence with patterns seen in other species' varieties, and reproductive compatibility in hybrids rather than relying on superficial contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply thorough anatomical and empirical study rather than superficial impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater number of the contrasts which were formerly supposed to exist have disappeared before the laborious researches of Tiedemann on the brain ... and the anatomical investigations of Vrolik and Weber on the form of the pelvis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on detailed anatomical, physiological, and empirical investigations to test claimed differences between populations; avoid overinterpreting visible traits without rigorous study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise caution using linguistic evidence for descent due to cultural and historical processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive ethnographical studies, based on a thorough knowledge of history, teach us that much caution should be applied in entering into these comparisons of nations, and of the languages employed by them at certain epochs. Subjection, long association, the influence of a foreign religion, the blending of races ... have produced similarly recurring phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language as a clue to descent but control for historical phenomena (conquest, cultural assimilation, elite language shifts, bilingualism); combine philological data with historical and ethnographic context.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reconstructing historical biogeography, consider staggered arrivals, glacial effects, and gradual change
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbes' synthesis: the flora and fauna of a region may have originated since the Miocene; assemblages did not appear simultaneously but at distinct times; composition includes forms from before, during, and after the glacial epoch; many species migrated over continuous land before/during/after glacial epochs; changes were gradual, not sudden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconstructing regional biogeographic history should consider timing of arrivals, multiple migration episodes, glacial/interglacial dynamics, source centers beyond the area, diffusion over land connections, and gradual transitions rather than abrupt replacements. Use geological and paleontological evidence in tandem with botanical/zoological data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat moral and political judgments about races with equality and universal human rights
rubrics_metrics.description: While we maintain the unity of the human species, we at the same time repel the depressing assumption of superior and inferior races of men. There are nations more susceptible of cultivation ... but none in themselves nobler than others. All are in like degree designed for freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative principle: scientific descriptions of human variation should not be used to justify hierarchies of worth or denial of freedom; adopt the recognition of common humanity as a guiding social and historical principle.
